title: erpax — a zero-entropy, content-addressed ERP corpus
description:
erpax is an ERP corpus in which every folder under src/ is one irreducible atom told three ways (form · code · proof), wired through a single content-uuid. Its law is zero entropy ⇒ infinite tamper-cost: a claim is enforced by a gate that blocks its violation, never by prose that asks for compliance.

Machine-checked proof, as of v1.0.6. The decisions that carry consequences are defined in Lean and proved there, with the TypeScript as a checked twin. Each twin’s test reads its .lean file for every theorem name it relies on, so a theorem cannot quietly disappear.

The inventory, kernel-checked with Lean Lean (version 4.33.1, arm64-apple-darwin24.6.0, commit 819816b2e0a3bf405af45ae5c7af2491d8f5bee6, Release) and counted rather than asserted: 200 theorems across 21 files, every one accepted by the kernel and none resting on sorry. 125 depend on no axioms at all (closed by decide over a stated finite domain); 75 rest on Lean’s own propext and Quot.sound. None uses native_decide, which would trust the compiler instead of the kernel. The record is addressed by the content hash of the sources it ran over, 5e89887c35fe1204, so a stale claim is detectable by construction.

The corpus holds 3620 content-addressed atoms.

The enforcement surface, counted from the sealed record rather than asserted. 21 down-only guardians hold the tree, each with a ceiling that can only FALL: a change that makes an axis worse fails the push, and a change that makes it better is sealed in the same commit that earns it. 5 of those ceilings are ZERO — a theorem rather than a tolerance, where no acceptable number exists: folder-name, accounting-structure, forbidden-intermediate, import-purity, phrase-without-diamond. The ceilings are addressed by ac211368-34cb-8e2a-8211-d372dfbb1223, sealed 2026-09-25. A guardian proves its own axis has not got worse — never that the corpus is correct.

What is proved, and what is not. A theorem proves its DECISION, never the facts it is fed: no proof here makes a red build green, a forged digest verify, or a divergent computation convergent, and none of it claims a Millennium problem is solved.
